class ParsingError(Error):
    """Raised when a configuration file does not follow legal syntax."""

    def __init__(self, source):
        super().__init__(f'Source contains parsing errors: {source!r}')
        self.source = source
        self.errors = []
        self.args = (source, )

    def append(self, lineno, line):
        self.errors.append((lineno, line))
        self.message += '\n\t[line %2d]: %s' % (lineno, line)


class MissingSectionHeaderError(ParsingError):
    """Raised when a key-value pair is found before any section header."""

    def __init__(self, filename, lineno, line):
        Error.__init__(
            self,
            'File contains no section headers.\nfile: %r, line: %d\n%r' %
            (filename, lineno, line))
        self.source = filename
        self.lineno = lineno
        self.line = line
        self.args = (filename, lineno, line)


class MultilineContinuationError(ParsingError):
    """Raised when a valueless option is followed by an indented line."""

    def __init__(self, source, lineno, line):
        ParsingError.__init__(self, source)
        self.append(lineno, line)
        self.lineno = lineno
        self.line = line
        self.args = (source, lineno, line)


# Used in parser getters to indicate the default behaviour when a specific
# option is not found it to raise an exception. Created to enable `None` as
# a valid fallback value.

class MultilineContinuationBackportTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_valueless_continuation_reports_location(self):
        source = "[service]\nflag\n    continued\n"
        for reader in ("read_string", "read_file"):
            with self.subTest(reader=reader):
                parser = configparser.ConfigParser(allow_no_value=True)
                body = io.StringIO(source) if reader == "read_file" else source
                with self.assertRaises(configparser.MultilineContinuationError) as caught:
                    getattr(parser, reader)(body, source="customer.ini")
                error = caught.exception
                self.assertEqual((error.source, error.lineno, error.line),
                                 ("customer.ini", 3, "    continued\n"))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

.. exception:: MultilineContinuationError(source, lineno, line)

   In this backport, raised when a key without a value is followed by a
   non-comment continuation line indented more deeply than the key. This is a
   subclass of :exc:`ParsingError`. It applies when *allow_no_value* is true;
   ordinary multiline values and valueless keys without a continuation remain
   supported.

   The attributes ``source``, ``lineno`` and ``line`` retain the supplied source
   name, one-based line number and exact offending line. The three constructor
   arguments are preserved when the exception is copied or pickled.
